items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: And Carl Burnett was the drummer at the time... I could really see the impact... We got paid extra for driving the van, plus doing the loading. Well, that was perfect for Carl, and I could use the extra dough... Anyhow, it was good working for Cal.

ctx.x: No, I met most of those guys for the first time, all but Carl, and I can't remember any of the other players. But they were local, the better players around. And Bateman came up, because he knew, he was standing tall and strong because he was ready to play. He wasn't afraid of me. Carl Perkins, he wasn't.

That was enough to start the thing off, and we had this drummer and...oh, I'm sorry. Carl wasn't the piano player on that set. Because what they did to me -- and I knew they did it deliberately, which was all dumb -- the guy started out with "Cherokee," real fast. I mean, "Cherokee" was so fast the drummer couldn't hardly keep time.
